Add set-relation helpers to SpecifierSet that compare the versions two sets accept, not the specifier objects themselves:

```python
>>> SpecifierSet(">=3.12,<3.13").is_subset(SpecifierSet(">=3.12"))
True
>>> SpecifierSet(">=3.12").is_subset(SpecifierSet(">=3.12,<3.13"))
False
>>> SpecifierSet(">=3.12").is_superset(SpecifierSet(">=3.12,<3.13"))
True
>>> SpecifierSet("<3.12").is_disjoint(SpecifierSet(">=3.12"))
True
>>> SpecifierSet("<3.12").is_disjoint(SpecifierSet(">=3.11"))
False
```

```python
def is_subset(self, other: SpecifierSet) -> bool:
    """Return whether every version matching this set also matches other."""
def is_superset(self, other: SpecifierSet) -> bool:
    """Return whether every version matching other also matches this set."""
def is_disjoint(self, other: SpecifierSet) -> bool:
    """Return whether this set and other share no matching versions."""
```

## Contract (also checked)
- The answers follow the accepted versions, including pre-release handling, exactly as SpecifierSet.to_range() describes them.
- Both sets must have been given the same `prereleases` argument, not just the same derived `prereleases` value (unset on one side counts as different); otherwise raise ValueError whose message mentions "pre-release".
- Sets containing `===` specifiers are rejected with ValueError (on either side) whose message mentions "==="; callers can use to_range() on both sides for those.
- An `other` that is not a SpecifierSet raises TypeError whose message mentions "SpecifierSet".
